classification_semantics.PURE_AGENTIC: The substantive decision is delegated to open-ended LLM reasoning. Generic tool transport, schema checks and logging alone do not make a node hybrid. No current registered operational entity is assigned this mode.
classification_semantics.PURE_ALGORITHMIC: Substantive decisions and state changes follow specified numerical methods, predicates, solvers or state machines without runtime LLM judgment. External observations can be uncertain; this does not make the decision agentic.
classification_semantics.HYBRID: LLM interpretation affects a proposal or assessment, while substantive numerical policy and deterministic admission jointly determine the accepted result. Aggregate containers inherit this mode from their children.

coverage_rule: Exactly one entry for every active non-edge entity in scope. Retired VIDs remain tombstones. Edges are deterministic routing/transition rules, not independent decision makers.
implementation_boundary: These are architecture decisions, not claims of completed implementation or grants of live trading authority.
broker_mutation_authority: Only the deterministic Command Commit Guard may admit a mutation, using valid upstream authority and injected ledger/broker dependencies. No LLM receives a direct broker mutation path.
change_policy: Changing decision mode, LLM authority or a supporting contract requires an explicit architecture revision and renewed validation; a different orchestrator or model choice does not silently change mode.

entries.name: Execution Engine
entries.rationale: Converge exact, approved economic intent to authoritative broker state through explicit numerical policies and state machines. The selected baseline has no unresolved semantic task for an LLM.
entries.registry_context: Broker-neutral Execution Engine: Margin Optimization -> Execution Slicing -> Optimal Execution, with cross-cutting State Integrity, Execution Recovery/Ledger and Interrupt Control.

entries.name: Active Instrument Execution Registry
entries.rationale: Maintain versioned economic requirements, confirmed effects and remaining work with scoped concurrency control. Supersession and cancellation cannot depend on language-model interpretation.
entries.registry_context: Holds outstanding instrument-level economic requirements with Runtime Intent Identity/version. Registry entries are persistent requirements, not broker order tickets.

entries.name: Broker Execution Port
entries.rationale: Validate and transport provider-neutral commands, queries and streams; normalize outcomes while leaving execution policy in the engine.
entries.registry_context: Broker-neutral interface implemented by unnumbered provider plug-ins such as Dhan, Kotak, or ICICI Securities.

entries.name: Normalized Broker Execution Facts
entries.rationale: Schema validation and serialization are algorithmic. The economic judgment, if any, belongs to the producing box; this record carries its validated result and provenance without adding discretion.
entries.registry_context: Authoritative broker order/fill/status/account facts normalized through the Broker Execution Port for execution components and upstream strategies. Provider response envelopes are implemented; component-specific execution-state aggregation remains active design.

entries.name: Live Market Execution State
entries.rationale: Schema validation and serialization are algorithmic. The economic judgment, if any, belongs to the producing box; this record carries its validated result and provenance without adding discretion.
entries.registry_context: Continuously refreshed normalized quotes, executable depth/order book, spread, freshness and tradability used by optimal execution.

entries.name: Live Broker Account State
entries.rationale: Schema validation and serialization are algorithmic. The economic judgment, if any, belongs to the producing box; this record carries its validated result and provenance without adding discretion.
entries.registry_context: Authoritative dynamic account-capacity state including cash/collateral/margin, current positions and pending orders relevant to execution feasibility.

entries.name: Hedge / Offset Relationship Analyzer
entries.rationale: Derive coverage and offsets from typed instrument/payoff relationships, current positions and authoritative margin facts. Unsupported instruments remain unsupported; an LLM cannot certify a hedge.
entries.registry_context: Infers structural risk-offset and coverage relationships from instruments, current positions and desired actions without strategy labels.

entries.name: Execution Dependency Graph
entries.rationale: Schema validation and serialization are algorithmic. The economic judgment, if any, belongs to the producing box; this record carries its validated result and provenance without adding discretion.
entries.registry_context: Quantity-aware precedence constraints derived from inferred hedge relationships.

entries.name: Margin Sequence Optimizer
entries.rationale: Search feasible intermediate execution states under explicit margin, coverage and quantity constraints. Emit ORDERED or UNCONSTRAINED only with a verifiable feasibility basis.
entries.registry_context: Produces the Execution Ordering Plan. It decides whether precedence constraints exist. If required, emits ORDERED with sequence/quantity constraints; if genuinely unnecessary, emits UNCONSTRAINED.

entries.name: Optimal Execution
entries.rationale: Run the specified algorithm on released slices under deterministic ordering, quantity, integrity and interrupt constraints.
entries.registry_context: Third normal-flow Execution Engine sub-box, after Margin Optimization and Execution Slicing. Enforces inherited ordering and slice-release constraints, then converts only released slice work plus live LOB/order state into time-indexed order-management actions.

entries.name: Eligible Execution Work Set
entries.rationale: Schema validation and serialization are algorithmic. The economic judgment, if any, belongs to the producing box; this record carries its validated result and provenance without adding discretion.
entries.registry_context: Current execution slice(s) released after ordering and slicing constraints. Contains intent identity/version, slice identity, instrument, side and permitted quantity. Optimal Execution acts only within this set.

entries.name: Temporal Execution Controller
entries.rationale: Drive timers and broker events, invoke the selected execution algorithm, validate its output and submit only through the guard; stale or delayed work is rejected.
entries.registry_context: Runs the time-indexed micro-execution loop, invokes the selected algorithm, validates its action, sends broker-neutral actions and consumes broker feedback.

entries.name: Execution Algorithm Port
entries.rationale: A typed plugin boundary exposes only eligible work and permitted actions. A future agentic plugin would require a new decision review; the current binding is Passive Chase.
entries.registry_context: Plug-and-play broker-neutral micro-execution interface. Algorithms receive only the work set released under the upstream ordering decision.

entries.name: Temporal Execution Decision
entries.rationale: Schema validation and serialization are algorithmic. The economic judgment, if any, belongs to the producing box; this record carries its validated result and provenance without adding discretion.
entries.registry_context: Time-t action: WAIT, PLACE_LIMIT, REPRICE_LIMIT, CANCEL_LIMIT, or PLACE_MARKET, with applicable quantity, price and order-reference fields.

entries.name: Margin Optimization
entries.rationale: Solve numerical path feasibility and ordering using typed instruments and broker-backed account capacity. Difficulty or combinatorial complexity does not imply a need for an LLM.
entries.registry_context: First Execution Engine sub-box. Determines hedge/margin dependencies and releases only currently eligible instrument quantity to Optimal Execution.

entries.name: Passive Chase
entries.rationale: The documented BUY-bid/SELL-ask, wait T, evaluate at most N intervals, cancel/reconcile and market-remainder policy is a complete state-machine specification.
entries.registry_context: Current default Optimal Execution plug-in. Posts passively at the same-side best quote, waits T, uses up to N passive waiting/evaluation intervals (at most N-1 refresh opportunities), then cancels/reconciles and markets the confirmed remainder.

entries.name: Passive Chase Parameters
entries.rationale: Schema validation and serialization are algorithmic. The economic judgment, if any, belongs to the producing box; this record carries its validated result and provenance without adding discretion.
entries.registry_context: T = passive waiting interval between evaluations; N = maximum passive waiting/evaluation intervals including the final fallback evaluation (at most N-1 refresh opportunities). Values intentionally TBD.

entries.name: Passive Chase State
entries.rationale: Persist and reduce typed events through explicit transitions. Only validated owning-component events may update this state; free-form LLM output cannot write authoritative state directly.
entries.registry_context: Working order reference, confirmed remaining quantity, passive-cycle count, last passive price and last evaluation time.

entries.name: Passive Reprice Timer
entries.rationale: Use the injected clock to schedule T, enforce cycle counters and cancel stale callbacks. LLM latency must not control repricing.
entries.registry_context: Waits parameter T between passive execution evaluations. Exact T is configuration, not architecture.

entries.name: Execution Ordering Plan
entries.rationale: Schema validation and serialization are algorithmic. The economic judgment, if any, belongs to the producing box; this record carries its validated result and provenance without adding discretion.
entries.registry_context: Mandatory Margin Optimization output declaring ORDERED or UNCONSTRAINED execution. ORDERED supplies explicit precedence/sequence constraints; UNCONSTRAINED explicitly declares that no ordering constraint exists.

entries.name: Ordering Constraint Enforcer
entries.rationale: Release only work permitted by the dependency graph and confirmed predecessor effects. Missing or invalid ordering permits no execution.
entries.registry_context: Interprets the Execution Ordering Plan. In ORDERED mode it releases only currently permitted step(s); in UNCONSTRAINED mode it releases all otherwise eligible work without imposing sequence. Missing/invalid ordering decision means no execution.

entries.name: Interrupt Control
entries.rationale: Emergency preemption, priority, cancellation, flattening and persistent latching follow fixed rules and must remain available when an LLM is unavailable.
entries.registry_context: NVIC-inspired supervisory sub-box. Orthogonal to the normal Margin Optimization -> Execution Slicing -> Optimal Execution chain and authorized to preempt all three according to interrupt priority.

entries.name: Interrupt Directive
entries.rationale: Schema validation and serialization are algorithmic. The economic judgment, if any, belongs to the producing box; this record carries its validated result and provenance without adding discretion.
entries.registry_context: Broker-neutral interrupt input carrying interrupt_id, level, scope, reason/source, issue time and target position/order scope. Levels currently: L1 CANCEL_WORK, L2 FLATTEN_SCOPE, L3 FLATTEN_ALL.

entries.name: Interrupt Arbiter
entries.rationale: Validate scope and authority, enforce L3 > L2 > L1 > normal, and prevent downgrade or unauthorized latch clearing.
entries.registry_context: Prioritizes and vectors interrupts. Higher levels preempt lower levels; normal execution is lower priority than every interrupt.

entries.name: Latched Interrupt State
entries.rationale: Persist and reduce typed events through explicit transitions. Only validated owning-component events may update this state; free-form LLM output cannot write authoritative state directly.
entries.registry_context: Persists active/pending interrupt priority, scope and completion state. Prevents normal convergence from recreating cancelled work until the interrupt is explicitly cleared.

entries.name: Interrupt Action Plan
entries.rationale: Schema validation and serialization are algorithmic. The economic judgment, if any, belongs to the producing box; this record carries its validated result and provenance without adding discretion.
entries.registry_context: Deterministic emergency handler output: cancel working orders, flatten explicit scope, or flatten all controlled positions. Emergency flatten uses market actions for confirmed net positions after cancellation/reconciliation.

entries.name: Runtime Intent Identity
entries.rationale: Schema validation and serialization are algorithmic. The economic judgment, if any, belongs to the producing box; this record carries its validated result and provenance without adding discretion.
entries.registry_context: Runtime identity carried by each live execution requirement: composition_id, execution mount_id, canonical component/VID context, intent_id, intent_version, supersedes_version/status and timestamps. The composition/mount context disambiguates concurrent uses of the same canonical execution component. Runtime identity remains distinct from immutable architectural CVIDs/BVIDs.

entries.name: Execution Slicing
entries.rationale: Transform already-permitted quantity into bounded slices while conserving quantity and precedence. The current one-slice sequential policy needs no judgment.
entries.registry_context: Normal-flow sub-box between Margin Optimization and Optimal Execution. Converts ordered/unconstrained eligible quantity into one or more execution slices. Default slice_count=1.

entries.name: Slice Planner
entries.rationale: Implement slice_count=1 and SEQUENTIAL first. Later numerical impact or liquidity optimization can remain algorithmic with explicit constraints and reproducible policy versions.
entries.registry_context: Chooses number, quantity and scheduling of execution slices while preserving upstream ordering constraints. Current default: one slice; if multiple slices exist, execute sequentially.

entries.name: Execution Slice Plan
entries.rationale: Schema validation and serialization are algorithmic. The economic judgment, if any, belongs to the producing box; this record carries its validated result and provenance without adding discretion.
entries.registry_context: Per-intent slice plan carrying intent identity/version, ordering metadata, slice_count, slice_id/index, quantity and scheduling policy.

entries.name: Slice Progress State
entries.rationale: Persist and reduce typed events through explicit transitions. Only validated owning-component events may update this state; free-form LLM output cannot write authoritative state directly.
entries.registry_context: Tracks current/complete/pending slices and authoritative filled quantity. Default sequential policy releases the next slice only after the current slice completes/reconciles.

entries.name: Slice Policy
entries.rationale: Schema validation and serialization are algorithmic. The economic judgment, if any, belongs to the producing box; this record carries its validated result and provenance without adding discretion.
entries.registry_context: Slicing configuration. Current default: slice_count=1 and scheduling_mode=SEQUENTIAL. Future policies may dynamically size/schedule slices.

entries.name: Execution Recovery
entries.rationale: Coordinate durable admission and authoritative reconstruction after uncertainty. A model cannot substitute inferred broker state for verified orders, fills and positions.
entries.registry_context: Cross-cutting durable execution/reconciliation sub-box. Owns write-ahead action recording, runtime identity/version validation, correlation and restart/ambiguity recovery.

entries.name: Execution Ledger
entries.rationale: Persist action/correlation identity and state transitions before broker release, enforce atomic uniqueness, and recover history after restart; broker observations remain authoritative.
entries.registry_context: Durable append/update record linking composition/mount/canonical execution context -> runtime intent/version -> slice -> execution action -> correlation/order IDs -> authoritative fills/status/positions. Canonical VIDs are never repurposed as runtime IDs.

entries.name: Reconciliation Engine
entries.rationale: Reconcile ledger entries against authoritative orders, trades and positions; deduplicate facts, resolve races and preserve ambiguity when evidence is insufficient.
entries.registry_context: Reconstructs broker truth after timeout, ambiguity or restart using authoritative orders, trades, fills and positions. No blind mutation retry while outcome is unknown.

entries.name: Command Commit Guard
entries.rationale: Enforce current intent, interrupt compatibility, integrity permission, unique identity and durable write-ahead recording before broker release. No LLM may waive these predicates.
entries.registry_context: Final pre-broker mutation gate. Rejects stale intent versions, requires durable write-ahead record/correlation identity, checks interrupt latch and action-class integrity permission, then releases the command.

entries.name: Recovery State
entries.rationale: Persist and reduce typed events through explicit transitions. Only validated owning-component events may update this state; free-form LLM output cannot write authoritative state directly.
entries.registry_context: Tracks CLEAN, RECONCILING, AMBIGUOUS and RECOVERY_REQUIRED execution states. Normal new mutations are blocked while unresolved ambiguity exists in relevant scope.

entries.name: Execution Action Envelope
entries.rationale: Schema validation and serialization are algorithmic. The economic judgment, if any, belongs to the producing box; this record carries its validated result and provenance without adding discretion.
entries.registry_context: Broker-neutral mutation envelope carrying composition_id, execution mount_id, canonical execution context, action_id, origin/intent or interrupt identity, intent_version, slice_id, action_class, correlation_id and requested broker operation.

entries.name: Reconciliation Result
entries.rationale: Schema validation and serialization are algorithmic. The economic judgment, if any, belongs to the producing box; this record carries its validated result and provenance without adding discretion.
entries.registry_context: Authoritative reconciliation result mapping attempted actions to broker orders/trades/fills/positions and exact confirmed remaining requirement.

entries.name: State Integrity
entries.rationale: Compute action-specific permission from explicit freshness, completeness, consistency and recovery predicates.
entries.registry_context: Cross-cutting broker-neutral readiness guard that classifies freshness/completeness/consistency of market, account, order/fill and recovery state before actions are allowed.

entries.name: State Integrity Guard
entries.rationale: Apply the correct integrity requirements to normal adds, reductions, cancellations and emergency flattening. Missing required evidence denies the affected action.
entries.registry_context: Computes action-class-aware execution permission. Normal risk-adding work requires sufficiently fresh/complete state; emergency cancel/flatten uses separate minimum-integrity requirements and never silently falls back.

entries.name: Integrity Assessment
entries.rationale: Schema validation and serialization are algorithmic. The economic judgment, if any, belongs to the producing box; this record carries its validated result and provenance without adding discretion.
entries.registry_context: Assessment with status VALID/STALE/INCOMPLETE/INCONSISTENT/UNKNOWN plus per-action permissions and reasons.

entries.name: Integrity State
entries.rationale: Persist and reduce typed events through explicit transitions. Only validated owning-component events may update this state; free-form LLM output cannot write authoritative state directly.
entries.registry_context: Current freshness/completeness/consistency state of required broker-neutral inputs.
